To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
C1-inh inhibits T lymphocyte proliferation, the generation of cytotoxic T lympho-cytes, and the endogenous production and secretion of cytokines by T lymphocytes in vitro.
C1-inh is a regulator of T cell-mediated immune responses and that this regulation is mediated by the ability of C1-inhibitor to inhibit the generation of desLys beta2-micro-globulin.
C1-inh inhibits T cell proliferation, cytotoxic T lymphocite generation and the endogenous production and release of lymphokines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a regulatory function of beta2m on T cell-mediated immunity.
the role of beta2m and desLys58beta2m as mediators of immune responses.
the role of complement activation in T cell-mediated immune responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
C1-inh has a dual effect in the immune system, i) it inhibits complement activation, and ii) it inhibits T cell activation and proliferation.
C1-inh inhibits T cell proliferation, the development and function of cytotoxic T lymphoblasts and changes the cytokine pattern in vitro.
C1-inh is a potent regulator of the immune response.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the C1-inh/beta2m system is an important regulator of T cell proliferation and differentiation.
C1-inh inhibits the development of T cell immunity in vitro and in vivo.
C1-inh inhibits beta2m-cleavage by activated C1s, which in turn leads to the generation of the immune-regulatory desLys58beta2m.
The main takeaway from our work is that
C1-ester inhibitor is not only an inhibitor of the complement pathway but also a potent inhibitor of T cell activation.
C1-inh is a negative regulator of T cell-mediated immunity.
C1-inh has an immunoregulatory function and may be a useful drug in the treatment of inflammatory and autoimmune diseases.
